Scholars like Bhumika R have analyzed Naga literature, including Kire's works, 
within the framework of postcolonial literature. They have explored how Naga writers 
negotiate their cultural identities in the aftermath of colonialism. Ozukum, in 
particular, has contributed to the understanding of the younger generation’s dilemma 
to balance tradition and culture with contemporary aspirations. Nevertheless, these 
studies often focus on broader postcolonial themes or the challenges of the youth 
rather than the specific concept of cultural hybridity. 
 
In summary, the existing body of research on Easterine Kire’s and Sentilong Ozukum’s 
literature provides valuable insights into various aspects of their works. However, there is a 
noticeable research gap regarding the exploration of cultural hybridity as a central theme 
within their narratives. This study aims to address this gap by examining how Kire’s and 
Ozukum’s writings establish a unique space for cultural negotiation, where traditional Naga 
elements and modern influences harmonize, reshape, and coexist. By positioning their works 
 
within the framework of cultural hybridity, this research will contribute to a deeper 
understanding of the transformative potential of literature in postcolonial contexts and its role 
in shaping cultural identities, especially in the context of Naga culture and animism. 
Additionally, this research will also highlight the distinctive perspectives and challenges of 
the younger generation of Naga writers, such as Ozukum, who seek to express their cultural 
identity in a rapidly changing world. 
OBJECTIVE 
• To understand cultural hybridity in Naga context. 
• To enunciate animism as a way of life for the Nagas. 
• To understand how a foreign language has helped to shape and enrich the Naga 
narration. 
• To understand the linear relation of oral and written Naga tradition and customs. 
• To delve into the cultural gain from a postcolonial perspective. 
• To understand the importance of interstice Naga identity in the works of Easterine 
Kire and Sentilong Ozukum. 
• To understand the nascent art of story writing of Naga writers in the written form 
closely related with the oral tradition. 
• To bring forth the idea of negotiated modern cultural space that can accommodate the 
past, the present and the future. 
• To analyze the dynamics of cultural hybridity through the framework of animism. 
 
METHODOLOGY 
This study will consider sociological, historical, and previous research on Naga religion, 
culture, and literature (both oral and written). The research will be organized into five 
chapters. The introduction will discuss the role of cultural hybridity, drawing upon the works 
of Homi Bhaba, Stuart Hall, Gayatri Spivak, and Paul Gilroy, and position Easterine Kire's 
and Sentilong Ozukum’s work within this framework. The latest MLA style (9th edition)/ 
APA7th edition will be followed for the citations.  
 
 
 
Hypothesis 
• Literature creates an alternative realm for cultural hybridity to thrive, often unnoticed 
in everyday discourse. 
• Easterine Kire and Sentilong Ozukum's works serve as a platform where cultural 
elements are skillfully negotiated and harmonized through artistic expression. 
• Naga cultural hybridity, as depicted in these literary works, acts as a bridge between 
the past, present, and future of Naga culture. 
• The blending of traditional Naga elements with modern influences, facilitated by the 
English language, sustains and shapes Naga cultural identity. 
• The research aims to highlight how cultural hybridity in Naga literature offers a 
harmonious coexistence of indigenous spirituality, animism, and Christianity. 
• This synthesis reflects the complexities of Naga society and promotes social cohesion. 
• Literature plays a pivotal role in mediating cultural differences, creating a 
postcolonial hybrid cultural space. 
• The study emphasizes the transformative potential of literature in postcolonial 
contexts, showcasing its ability to preserve and adapt cultural identities. 
• Through the lens of Naga culture and animism, the research contributes to the 
understanding of how literature can preserve and enrich cultural heritage despite 
external influences and contemporary challenges. 
 
CHAPTERIZATION 
Chapter 1 
Introduction: Cultural Hybridity in Naga Literature 
• Setting the stage by introducing the concept of animism and cultural hybridity and its 
relevance in Naga literature. 
• Briefly summarizing the existing research gap and the need to explore this theme 
within Easterine Kire's and Sentilong Ozukum’s works. 
• Establishing the theoretical framework by drawing upon the works of scholars like 
Homi Bhaba, Stuart Hall, Gayatri Spivak, and Paul Gilroy. 
 
• Positioning Easterine Kire and Sentilong Ozukum’s literary contributions within the 
context of cultural hybridity. 
 
Chapter 2 
Naga Animism, Ecoethics and Synthesis of Tradition with Modernity 
• Examining the role of the English language in Naga literature and its impact on 
cultural hybridity. 
• Exploring how the use of English bridges traditional Naga storytelling with 
contemporary narratives in Kire's and Ozukum’s works. 
• Analyzing specific examples from their writings that illustrate language as a medium 
for cultural negotiation and expression. 
 
Chapter 3 
Religion and Traditional Practices: A Harmonious Blend in Kire and Ozukum’s Fiction 
• Investigating the relationship between religion and traditional practices in Naga 
society. 
• Examining how they skillfully blend elements of indigenous Naga spirituality, 
animism, and Christianity in their narratives. 
• Analyzing their portrayal of the coexistence and negotiation of these diverse belief 
systems within the characters and stories. 
 
Chapter 4 
 
Narrative Structure and Hybridity in Postcolonial Context 
• Delving into the narrative structures employed by Easterine Kire and Sentilong 
Ozukum in their works. 
• Exploring how their storytelling art mediates differences and creates a postcolonial 
hybrid cultural space. 
 
• Discussing the ways in which narrative techniques contribute to the portrayal of 
cultural hybridity in her narratives. 
 
Chapter 5 
Cultural Hybridity as a Catalyst for Social Cohesion 
• Reflecting on the implications of cultural hybridity in the context of Naga culture and 
animism. 
• Analyzing how the negotiation of cultural elements in Kire and Ozukum’s works 
contributes to social cohesion in Naga society. 
To discuss the broader significance of literature as a means of preserving and shaping 
cultural identities in postcolonial settings. 
 
Chapter 6: Conclusion 
 
The concluding chapter shall sum up all the preceding chapters and shall focus in precise 
ways in which cultural hybridity tinged with animism, mysticism and modern culture has 
changed the Naga way of life going into the future.

-- Fix Tree-sitter foldexpr freezing on every keystroke in Insert mode
local org_fold_group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("OrgFoldLagFix", { clear = true })

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("InsertEnter", {
  group = org_fold_group,
  pattern = { "*.org", "*.md" },
  callback = function()
    if vim.w.foldmethod_save == nil and vim.wo.foldmethod == "expr" then
      vim.w.foldmethod_save = "expr"
      vim.wo.foldmethod = "manual"
    end
  end,
})

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("InsertLeave", {
  group = org_fold_group,
  pattern = { "*.org", "*.md" },
  callback = function()
    if vim.w.foldmethod_save then
      vim.wo.foldmethod = vim.w.foldmethod_save
      vim.w.foldmethod_save = nil
    end
  end,
})
